meta.titre: Visible and Invisible Trade: goods, services and the balance of trade
meta.sous_theme: Visible and invisible imports and exports, and the trade balance

sections.contenu_markdown: A ship leaves a port loaded with cocoa for Europe. In the same week, foreign tourists pay hotel bills in Cameroon and a local company pays a foreign insurer. All three are foreign trade, but only the first can be seen being loaded. Examiners test whether you can classify each transaction as visible or invisible and as an import or an export, and whether you can use examples to distinguish them. This course shows how to do both and how the balance of trade is worked out.

items: Foreign trade is the buying and selling of goods and services between countries.
A country sells its exports to other countries and buys its imports from them.
A service is work done for someone, such as banking or transport, that is not a physical good.

sections.titre: Visible and invisible items of trade
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Imports and exports

An **export** is something sold to another country, so money comes **into** the exporting country. An **import** is something bought from another country, so money goes **out**.

### Visible and invisible

**Visible trade** is trade in physical goods. The goods can be seen, touched and counted, and they pass through ports, airports and customs posts, where they are recorded.

**Invisible trade** is trade in services. A service has no physical form and does not go through customs.

| | Visible | Invisible |
|---|---|---|
| Nature | Goods | Services |
| Exports (country earns) | Cocoa, coffee, timber sold abroad | Hotel and travel services bought by foreign tourists; shipping, banking or insurance services sold to foreigners |
| Imports (country pays) | Machines, vehicles, medicines bought from abroad | Premiums paid to a foreign insurer; fares paid to a foreign airline; fees paid to a school abroad |
| Recorded | At ports and borders by customs | Not by customs; it appears only in records of payments |

### The balance of trade

The **balance of trade** compares the value of visible exports with the value of visible imports:

$\text{Balance of trade} = \text{Visible exports} - \text{Visible imports}$

A positive result is a **surplus** (favourable); a negative result is a **deficit** (unfavourable). Invisible trade is left out of this figure, but a country may count it separately to see its full position.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you are given a transaction and asked to name it
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ask two questions. Is it a good or a service? Is the country receiving money (export) or paying money (import)? A foreign visitor paying for a hotel in your country is an **invisible export**. A local firm paying a foreign shipping line is an **invisible import**.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When both goods and services are given and the full position is asked
variantes.contenu_markdown: Work out the balance of trade for goods and the invisible balance separately, then add them. A deficit in goods can be reduced, or even removed, by a surplus in services such as tourism.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says 'using examples, distinguish between'
variantes.contenu_markdown: State what each term means, give at least one example of each, and add one point of contrast such as 'goods pass through customs, services do not'. A definition without an example loses marks.

sections.enonce_markdown: The foreign trade of Country Z in one year (hypothetical figures, in million FCFA) was: visible exports 640, visible imports 710, invisible exports 200, invisible imports 150. (a) Classify each of these transactions as visible or invisible and as an export or an import for Country Z: (i) timber sold to a buyer abroad, (ii) hotel bills paid by foreign tourists in Z, (iii) tractors bought from abroad, (iv) insurance premiums paid by a firm in Z to a foreign company. (b) Calculate the balance of trade. (c) Calculate the invisible balance and the combined balance.

etapes.justification: Decide whether it is a good or a service, then whether money enters or leaves Z.
etapes.resultat_markdown:
| Transaction | Class |
|---|---|
| (i) Timber sold abroad | Visible export |
| (ii) Hotel bills of foreign tourists | Invisible export |
| (iii) Tractors bought from abroad | Visible import |
| (iv) Premiums paid to a foreign insurer | Invisible import |

etapes.justification: It uses visible items only: exports minus imports.
Add the balance of trade and the invisible balance to see the full position on goods and services.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **The balance of trade is a deficit of 70 million FCFA; the invisible balance is a surplus of 50 million FCFA; the combined position is a deficit of 20 million FCFA.** The services sold abroad reduced the deficit in goods but did not remove it.

items.erreur_markdown: 'Visible exports are goods bought from abroad.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Goods bought from abroad are imports. Exports are sold to other countries.
items.correction_markdown: Visible exports: goods sold abroad. Visible imports: goods bought from abroad.

items.erreur_markdown: 'Invisible trade means secret or illegal trade such as smuggling.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Invisible trade is lawful trade in services. 'Invisible' only means that a service cannot be seen or touched.
items.correction_markdown: Invisible items are services such as banking, insurance, transport and tourism.

items.erreur_markdown: Classifying a foreign tourist's hotel bill as an import of the host country
items.pourquoi_faux: The host country is receiving foreign money for a service, so it is an export, an invisible one.
items.correction_markdown: Ask whether money comes into the country (export) or goes out (import).

items.erreur_markdown: Including services when calculating the balance of trade
items.pourquoi_faux: The balance of trade is made of visible items only. Services belong to the invisible balance.
items.correction_markdown: Use visible exports and visible imports for the balance of trade, then add the invisible balance if the full position is asked.

items.enonce_markdown: Classify each transaction as a visible export, visible import, invisible export or invisible import for Cameroon: (i) coffee sold to a foreign buyer, (ii) a Cameroonian family flying with a foreign airline, (iii) foreign visitors paying for guided tours in Cameroon, (iv) medicines bought from abroad, (v) a Cameroonian bank earning fees from a foreign company, (vi) a Cameroonian student paying fees at a foreign college.
items.solution_markdown: (i) **Visible export**. (ii) **Invisible import**: a service bought from a foreign firm. (iii) **Invisible export**: a service sold to foreigners. (iv) **Visible import**. (v) **Invisible export**. (vi) **Invisible import**.

items.enonce_markdown: A country had these foreign trade figures in million FCFA: visible exports 1250, visible imports 1430, invisible exports 380, invisible imports 290. (a) Calculate the balance of trade. (b) Calculate the invisible balance. (c) Calculate the combined balance and say whether it is a surplus or a deficit.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $1250 - 1430 =$ **-180 million FCFA** (deficit).

(b) $380 - 290 =$ **+90 million FCFA** (surplus).

(c) $-180 + 90 =$ **-90 million FCFA**, a **deficit** of 90 million FCFA.

items.enonce_markdown: Using examples, distinguish between visible and invisible trade, and explain TWO ways in which invisible exports help a country whose imports of goods are larger than its exports of goods. (8 marks)
items.solution_markdown:
Award marks as follows:

- Visible trade is trade in physical goods that can be seen and are recorded by customs; example: cocoa exported, vehicles imported (2 marks).
- Invisible trade is trade in services that cannot be seen or touched; example: tourism, banking, insurance and shipping (2 marks).
- Contrast: goods pass through customs, services do not (1 mark).
- Way 1: earnings from invisible exports, such as tourism and services sold to foreigners, bring in foreign money that helps to pay for the surplus of imported goods (1.5 marks).
- Way 2: invisible exports reduce the overall deficit, so the country needs to borrow less from abroad to pay for the goods it must import (1.5 marks).

items_markdown: **Visible** items are goods that can be seen and are recorded by customs; **invisible** items are services.
An **export** brings money into the country; an **import** takes money out.
A foreign tourist spending in your country is an invisible export for your country.
Balance of trade = visible exports - visible imports; it is a surplus if positive and a deficit if negative.
In a 'distinguish' question, give definitions, examples and a point of contrast.
